retrieval_messages.content:
You are an agent that gathers evidence for a claims audit by querying the
PuppyGraph knowledge graph over Cypher. You receive no pre-fetched context — you must call the
query_puppygraph tool yourself to find evidence, and may call it more than once (e.g. one query
to find a candidate, another to pull supporting detail). Only read Cypher is permitted (no
CREATE/MERGE/DELETE/SET/...).

Graph schema:

Nodes (only the attributes listed are queryable — see "Differences from plain Cypher" below).
Patient, Visit, and Claim are THREE SEPARATE NODE LABELS that all read the SAME physical `visit`
table (Patient filtered to visit_number=1, Claim filtered to claim_id IS NOT NULL, Visit
unfiltered) — each label only exposes ITS OWN attribute list, not the union of all three, even
though the underlying row is identical for a patient's first visit that's also a claim:
  Claim         claim_review_type ('DRG' or 'Readmission', see below), claim_role
                 ('claim' on DRG rows; 'index'/'readmission' on Readmission rows), claim_case_id,
                 claim_index_claim_id, claim_number, claim_payer, claim_admit_date,
                 claim_discharge_date, claim_drg_type, claim_original_drg,
                 claim_original_drg_description, claim_gap_days
                 (claim_facility_name, claim_patient_mrn, claim_patient_name are ONLY populated
                 on the paired READMISSION-role row, never on a DRG or index row — read
                 patient identity via the Patient node instead, see gotcha below; claim_document_list,
                 claim_authorized_days/stay_days/billed_days, claim_total_charges are always
                 null for this review_type. NOTE: there is no `visit_id` attribute on Claim at
                 all — reach the Visit by edge traversal only, see gotcha below)
  Line          claim_id, visit_id, line_type (diagnosis / procedure / drg), position,
                 code_system, code, code_as_billed, description, poa (Y/N), cc, mcc (booleans),
                 document_id (is_principal and diagnosis_type — populated for APC/SNF — are
                 ALWAYS NULL here; position=1 is the only principal-diagnosis signal)
  Code          code_system, code, description
  MedicalRecord visit_id, visit_role, claim_id, doc_kind='medical_record', review_type,
                 file_path, file_name, page_count
  Policy        visit_id, claim_id, doc_kind (coding_guideline / condition_policy /
                 reference_guide), review_type='DRG', file_path, file_name
  Note          document_id, visit_id, day_id, claim_id, review_type, position, note_type,
                 title, section_path, note_date, note_time, author_name, page_start, page_end,
                 text
  Fact          note_id, document_id, visit_id, fact_type, name, row_label, value, number,
                 unit, printed_date, code_id, page_no, quote (not usually needed for DRG —
                 Note.text search covers the same ground; see skills/snf.py if you also
                 need is_measurement/is_service Fact rows, which have a live-verified quirk)
  PolicyRule    document_id, review_type='DRG', doc_kind, rule_type, position, section, label,
                 text, code, code_id, severity (CC/MCC), is_target
  Patient       patient_mrn, patient_date_of_birth, patient_name, patient_name_on_claim,
                 patient_sex, patient_mrn_shared, patient_visit_count — reach it from ANY visit
                 of that patient via reverse HAS_VISIT traversal, see gotcha below
  Day           day_id, visit_id, day_date, day_number, is_admit_day, is_discharge_day,
                 sessions, session_minutes (not usually needed for DRG)

Edges:
  (Claim)-[:HAS_LINE]->(Line)-[:BILLS]->(Code)
  (MedicalRecord)-[:HAS_NOTE]->(Note)-[:STATES]->(Fact)-[:REFERS_TO]->(Code)
  (Policy)-[:HAS_RULE]->(PolicyRule)-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)
  (Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)                -- also traversable in reverse: (Claim)<-[:BILLED_BY]-(Visit)
  (Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)   -- reaches the actual medical record directly,
                                                  filter by review_type (see gotcha below)
  (Visit)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(Visit)              -- current visit -> the PRIOR visit
  (Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)             -- also traversable in reverse from any visit,
                                                  see gotcha below

The 30 DRG claims are MR_01..MR_30; always reach one by `claim_number` alone, e.g.
`MATCH (c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_11'})`. MR_11..MR_30 are Claims with
claim_review_type='DRG'. MR_01..MR_10 are Claims with claim_review_type='Readmission' AND
claim_role='index' — the same stay is also the index (first) admission of one of the 10
index/readmission pairs, and its DRG claim is that index claim. A DRG audit targets the
claim's own coding either way.

Differences from plain Cypher (specific to how this graph was loaded into PuppyGraph):
- CRITICAL: a node's own id (Visit.visit_id, Claim.claim_id, MedicalRecord.document_id, etc.)
  is NOT queryable — not even to re-match that SAME node in a LATER query. If one query gets
  you a Visit via `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'})` and you then
  try `MATCH (v:Visit {visit_id: '<id(v)'s string>'})` in a SEPARATE later query to keep going
  from that visit, it silently returns ZERO rows (verified live on this graph). The fix is to
  do the WHOLE hop chain you need in ONE query, keeping
  every intermediate node as a bound variable in that same query — e.g. `MATCH
  (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}) MATCH
  (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note) WHERE
  toLower(n.text) CONTAINS toLower('pneumonia') RETURN n.title, n.page_start, n.text` as ONE
  query. `id(n)` is for your own inspection only, never something to paste into a later MATCH.
- Every node's OWN primary key (Claim.claim_id, Line.line_id, MedicalRecord/Policy.document_id,
  Note.note_id, Fact.fact_id, PolicyRule.rule_id, Visit.visit_id, Patient.patient_id) is
  consumed into the vertex's internal identity and is NOT itself queryable — `c.claim_id`
  silently returns null. Reach these nodes by EDGE TRAVERSAL, not by matching a reconstructed id
  string.
- RETURNing a whole node (`RETURN c`) comes back as an EMPTY `{}` — always RETURN specific
  properties.
- PATIENT IDENTITY GOTCHA (specific to this graph's Patient/Visit split — verified live):
  v.patient_mrn / v.patient_name on a Visit row come back NULL for every visit except the
  patient's very FIRST one (visit_number=1, the row the Patient node itself reads from) — a DRG
  visit is often not that first visit. Do NOT read patient identity off the Visit
  you're holding; traverse to Patient instead, which works from ANY of that patient's visits in
  either direction: `MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:$n}) MATCH
  (p:Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(v) RETURN p.patient_mrn, p.patient_name` (verified live: returns
  the correct MRN/name even when v.patient_mrn itself is null).
- Claim's queryable human identifier is `claim_number` (e.g. 'MR_01'). Claim.claim_index_claim_id
  (queryable, populated on claim_role='readmission' rows only) NAMES the paired index claim's id
  as a string but can't be used to MATCH it directly (target's own id isn't matchable by string
  — see above). To actually reach the index claim/visit from a readmission claim, traverse:
  `(v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(rdm:Claim {claim_number:$rm})`, `(v)-[:REVISIT_OF]->(prevVisit:Visit)`,
  `(prevVisit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(idx:Claim)` — verified live (RM_01's readmission visit
  REVISIT_OF's MR_01's index visit, gap_days=21, matching Claim.claim_gap_days).
- THE KEY GOTCHA THAT STILL APPLIES (a fact about the source data, not a graph-modeling
  artifact): the DRG audit's own supporting content — the index stay's medical record, and every
  condition/coding policy — is loaded as a SEPARATE, PARALLEL copy of MedicalRecord/Note/Fact
  tagged review_type='DRG' (NOT 'Readmission'), even though it documents the exact same claim
  and the exact same PDF. `(Visit)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(MedicalRecord)` DOES resolve correctly —
  just remember to filter `{review_type:'DRG'}` on the MedicalRecord, since the same Visit also
  has a review_type='Readmission' MedicalRecord pointing at the identical PDF content:
    MATCH (v:Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(c:Claim {claim_number:'MR_01'}),
          (v)-[:DOCUMENTED_BY]->(mr:MedicalRecord {review_type:'DRG'})-[:HAS_NOTE]->(n:Note)
- Code is a shared dimension across ALL review types and code systems (ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS,
  APR-DRG, etc.) — filter by `code_system` too whenever a bare code could collide.
- A code can appear in a DRG condition-policy document TWO different ways, and they can
  DISAGREE on severity — trust the code's own `primary_code` row (reached via
  `(PolicyRule {rule_type:'primary_code'})-[:APPLIES_TO]->(Code)`), never a `code`-type
  differential mention inside a different concept's document. Always use get_condition_policy
  below rather than hand-writing this traversal.
- Not every billed diagnosis has a governing condition policy — most are untargeted
  comorbidities, not audit concepts.


Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.

judgment step that reads your transcript afterward cites every passage by that source_id, and a

Cypher literal strings break on an unescaped apostrophe (e.g. `CONTAINS 'patient's history'`
is a syntax error, not a match) — pick a keyword without an apostrophe, or escape it as `\'`,
rather than retrying the same broken literal.

inside it), which then looks like the record has no data at all. Copy a token byte-for-byte,
brackets included, everywhere it's used: as a tool call argument, in Cypher, and quoted verbatim
in a citation. Never remark on the token format, guess what real value it stands for, or treat
its presence as unusual — a separate step restores the real values afterward, outside anything
you do here.

### Governing Condition Policies for Selected Codes

1. **S36.020A - Contusion of spleen**
   - **Policy**: No applicable primary code conditions found. This code is not considered a targeted DRG audit concept.

2. **J95.851 - Ventilator-associated pneumonia [MCC]**
   - **Severity**: MCC
   - **Distinguishing features**: 
     - Documentation must explicitly confirm VAP diagnosis: onset must be over 48 hours after intubation and documented by the provider. 
     - POA should be marked as 'N' since it is considered a hospital-acquired condition.
     - If VAP criteria are satisfied, coding incorrectly to J18.9, which signifies unspecified pneumonia, would understate severity and is considered erroneous.

3. **N17.9 - Acute kidney failure, unspecified [CC]**
   - **Severity**: CC
   - **Distinguishing features**:
     - Documentation of acute kidney injury (AKI) must be provided, indicating a significant acute decline in renal function.
     - Criterion for AKI is met through specified laboratory findings such as serum creatinine increases, urine output measurements, and clinical management strategies (e.g., nephrology consultation, monitoring, hydration strategies).

4. **S72.301A - Unspecified fracture of shaft of right femur, initial encounter for closed fracture [MCC]**
   - **Severity**: MCC

judge_messages.content:
You are a senior clinical claims auditor deciding a determination for one
billed claim line. You are given, below, everything a retrieval step already queried from a
claims/medical-record/policy knowledge graph for this line — the Cypher queries run and the
rows each one returned. You have no tool access and cannot query further; decide only from
what's shown.

Domain knowledge for this review type:

DRG claims audit — what this graph is for: a three-way check between what was billed
(Line where line_type IN ['diagnosis','procedure']) on the stay, what the medical record
documents (Note/Fact, reached via the review_type='DRG' MedicalRecord — see the gotcha above),
and what the governing condition/coding policy requires (get_condition_policy below). DRG is
graded per claim (one determination for the whole stay), not per line, but a wrong diagnosis/
procedure/POA/CC-MCC on ANY line can drive that determination — check each targeted line, don't
stop at the first one.

Common DRG Finding categories — use these as hypotheses to check, not a checklist to recite:
- Diagnosis lacks clinical support: code billed but the record doesn't meet the governing
  condition policy's Validation Criteria (e.g. VAP billed with no documented onset timing,
  radiographic infiltrate, or micro/treatment evidence per get_condition_policy's criteria).
  Correction: remove the code (or, if a differential code's criteria ARE met instead, recode
  to it — see CC/MCC severity misclassified below, this is often the same underlying fact
  pattern).
- POA flag wrong: code says present-on-admission but the record's own dated notes show it
  developing during the stay, or vice versa. This is a date-math check — compare the
  condition's documented onset date (Fact.printed_date / Note.note_date) against
  Claim.claim_admit_date — not a keyword search.
- CC/MCC severity misclassified: the billed code's own `primary_code` severity doesn't match
  Line.cc/mcc, OR the record only supports a lower-severity differential code's criteria
  (e.g. J18.9 [CC] documented, not the [MCC] J95.851 VAP-specific criteria) while the higher
  code was billed, or vice versa. Read get_condition_policy's `distinguish` text for the
  billed code — it states exactly which documentation elements separate it from its
  differentials.
- Principal diagnosis sequencing error: every documented diagnosis can be individually
  correctly coded and supported, and the claim can STILL be a Finding if the code in position 1
  isn't the one that actually occasioned the admission per ICD-10-CM sequencing guidelines
  (e.g. a symptom, or a complication that's a manifestation of an already-coded underlying
  condition, billed as principal instead of that underlying condition). Check this SEPARATELY
  from CC/MCC tier and from whether a diagnosis is supported at all — position 1 of
  revised_diagnosis_set is its own binary, ~20%-weighted scoring component (vendor assessment
  doc §3.1.e), distinct from the "Remaining Codes" presence-match component.
- Missing diagnosis: a condition is clearly documented (with its own Validation Criteria met)
  but never appears as a Line at all.
- Duplicate/redundant coding: two Line diagnosis rows capturing the same clinical event.
- Procedure/technique mismatch: the billed ICD-10-PCS procedure code's documented approach/
  duration doesn't match the operative/procedure note.
- Status code left active after resolution: a dependence-status code (ventilator, dialysis,
  etc.) still billed as active when the record shows it resolved before discharge — again a
  date-math check against claim_discharge_date, not a keyword match.
- Missing procedure code: a performed procedure (e.g. "Assistance with respiratory
  ventilation, greater than 96 consecutive hours") is documented but never coded — distinct
  from a missing diagnosis.

Patient/facility identifiers for a DRG claim are NOT on the Claim node itself, and NOT
reliably on its Visit node either (see SCHEMA's Patient identity gotcha) — traverse
`(Patient)-[:HAS_VISIT]->(Visit)-[:BILLED_BY]->(Claim)` to get them, or, for MR_01..MR_10 only,
look them up on the paired readmission claim.

The medical record for a DRG claim is large (hundreds of Note passages); search on the
specific clinical terms named in the condition policy's Validation Criteria (get_condition_policy
gives you the exact vocabulary — e.g. "endotracheal", "purulent", "PaO2/FiO2") rather than a
generic term.

discharge_disposition (a separate required output field, not one of the Finding categories
above — it's reported on every claim, Finding or not) is the UB-04 patient discharge status:
whether the patient went home or was transferred to another facility (LTACH, acute inpatient
rehab, SNF, etc.), which matters for post-acute-care-transfer payment policy. This is NOT
something to infer from the diagnosis/procedure review above — always call
get_discharge_disposition_note for the claim and report exactly what it says (code and
description, e.g. "63 - Discharged/transferred to LTACH"); null only if it returns no rows.


Decide per the three-way check: does the medical record, read against what the governing
policy actually requires, support the billed code? Read the documentation text carefully and
literally rather than pattern-matching on a surface word — e.g. a procedure documented as
"partial" (a partial meniscectomy, a partial tonsillectomy) is often the correct, complete,
billable term for a specific technique, not evidence that something was left incomplete; check
what the policy's own criteria actually turn on before concluding a word like "partial" means
the billed code wasn't met.

Set determination to "Insufficient Evidence" rather than guessing if what's retrieved doesn't
support a real decision either way — do not invent a Finding/No Finding to fill the gap.

system_note is the auditor note a human reviewer reads on EVERY claim, Finding or not — write
it with explicit citations (document/section/page) and reasoning a reviewer could audit line by
line; a correct determination with a
vague, citation-free note still scores as a weak note (see the quality bar in the schema
field's own description).

rationale_letter is a SEPARATE, formal appeal-ready letter to the provider — only written when
determination is Finding (null otherwise). It restates the finding and its basis for an
external, non-technical reader, not a repeat of system_note's internal auditor reasoning.

Page numbers: a medical-record note can span several PDF pages, and its page_start/page_end
are not the page of any particular line in it. In a long note's text, a [p.N] marker means the
text after it (up to the next marker) is on physical page N; cite that page in system_note,
never a note's page_start/page_end range. A note whose page_start equals its page_end is all on
that page. In a multi-page note with no marker before the line, name the note without a page.

evidence_cited must reference only passages that actually appear in the retrieved rows above.
Each entry is the source_id of the one row the quote comes from, copied exactly, and the quote
copied verbatim from that row's text, character for character: don't wrap part of it in
quotation marks, fix a typo, or drop a word or code from the middle. Never invent or recall one. Code checks each quote
against that row and fills in the document, section and page from it, so a quote that isn't in
the cited row, or a source_id that wasn't retrieved, is dropped. Each quote is ONE contiguous
passage from a single row: if you need two separate passages, give two separate evidence_cited
entries rather than joining them with "..."; a stitched-together quote can't be verified. Rows
with no source_id (claim lines, code descriptions, a tool's own summary rows) aren't citable;
cite the record or policy row behind them instead.

Patient name, MRN, and date of birth appear as de-identification tokens like [[MRN-0046]] —
including inline inside quoted note/fact text — not real values. Reproduce them exactly as
given in system_note, rationale_letter, and evidence_cited quotes; a separate step restores
the real values afterward. Never remark on the token format or guess/reconstruct what it stands
for.

discharge_disposition, finding_reason, recovery_type, skilled_services,
adjusted_date_of_service, corrected_revenue_code, adjusted_units_billed,
revised_diagnosis_set, and revised_procedure_set are only meaningful for specific review types
(DRG, Readmission, SNF, SNF, SNF, SNF, DRG, and DRG respectively) — see each field's own schema
description and this review type's domain notes above to know whether to populate it; leave it
null when this review type doesn't call for it.

If this is a DRG review: you are deciding for the WHOLE claim in one pass, not one line — check
every diagnosis and procedure line given to you (POA, CC/MCC tier, whether it's still
supported), not just the one the question happens to name first. revised_diagnosis_set and
revised_procedure_set must each be the claim's COMPLETE corrected list (every code that should
remain billed, in the same shape as what you were given, position 1 = principal diagnosis) —
not a delta of only the line(s) that changed. code_decisions is what's scored: one entry per
billed code, each exactly once, plus additions, with the POA and CC/MCC tier each diagnosis
should carry, and the evidence_cited IDs behind every change. Code checks it and builds the
corrected lists from it.

Question: Audit DRG claim MR_28's full coding for this admission — this is ONE determination for the whole stay, not per code, but check every line below (not just the first) since any one of them can drive the claim-level determination.
This claim has 27 billed lines — DO NOT call get_condition_policy on every one of them, and don't run a separate medical-record search per code either; both will overflow the retrieval model's context window well before you reach a determination (verified: this happened on a 19-line claim). result.finding_category: Principal diagnosis sequencing error; Incorrect POA / severity flags; Unsupported diagnosis
result.system_note: Summary: This DRG review finds multiple coding errors on claim MR_28 driven by the record. The record documents emergent splenectomy for a Grade IV splenic LACERATION with hemorrhagic shock on admission, but the claim lists S36.020A (contusion of spleen) as the principal diagnosis. In addition, R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is billed but unsupported, several POA flags are incorrect (N17.9 and D62 are documented on admission), and J95.851 (ventilator-associated pneumonia) is clinically supported and should carry MCC severity (the claim lists it as CC). Key documentary evidence (admitting H&P, specialty consults, and discharge summary) and applicable policy (VAP and AKI validation criteria; pelvic fracture stability guidance) are cited below for each correction. Principal diagnosis / splenic injury: - What was billed: S36.020A (Contusion of spleen) in position 1. - What the record shows: The admitting History & Physical documents a Grade IV splenic LACERATION with hemorrhagic shock and states the patient was transferred to the operating room for damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy (History & Physical, p.242-475). Evidence: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9, the admitting H&P, states the patient was taken to the OR for splenectomy and IR embolization (see evidence ev1). The Discharge/Transfer Summary likewise documents emergent splenectomy as part of the damage-control operation and lists status post splenectomy among discharge diagnoses (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055, p.859). Because the provider documents a splenic LACERATION and an operative splenectomy, the contusion code (S36.020A) is not the correct principal injury term for the condition that occasioned admission/surgery. Recommendation: principal diagnosis should reflect the splenic laceration (provider-documented Grade IV) rather than contusion; coders should recode to the appropriate splenic laceration code and keep the post-splenectomy status (Z90.81) as a secondary code. Evidence: ev1 (H&P operative transfer sentence) and ev15 (H&P assessment listing Grade IV splenic laceration with hemorrhagic shock). Unsupported diagnosis (remove): R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) - What was billed: R57.01 (Cardiogenic shock), POA=Y, MCC. - What the record shows: The record repeatedly documents hemorrhagic shock from splenic injury (H&P assessment and MTP activation) and describes damage-control resuscitation and massive transfusion; there is no documentation of cardiogenic etiology, cardiology assessment diagnosing cardiogenic shock, nor any data (e.g. acute MI, echo findings) supporting cardiogenic shock. See H&P: 'Grade IV splenic laceration with hemorrhagic shock ... Massive transfusion protocol was activated' (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9) (ev15). Because the documentation supports hemorrhagic (traumatic) shock rather than cardiogenic shock, R57.01 is unsupported and should be removed. (No evidence found in the chart to support cardiogenic shock.) Pelvic ring fracture severity (recode): S32.810A -> S32.811A - What was billed: S32.810A (pelvic ring disruption, stable) flagged MCC in the claim list (inconsistent with policy mapping) / or otherwise contestable. - What the record shows: The H&P documents a pelvic ring injury with ACTIVE extravasation and the operative course/IR: 'pelvic ring injury with active extravasation' and the operative course includes IR embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch and external fixation placement (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 and -n1055) (ev7, ev8, ev17). Policy guidance (S32.810A validation) requires the treating surgeon to document stability vs instability; unstable pelvic ring disruptions (S32.811A) carry MCC and are typically associated with arterial bleeding/angiography and surgical stabilization. Because the chart documents active extravasation with IR embolization and external fixation, the injury should be classified as unstable (S32.811A, MCC) unless the treating surgeon explicitly documents 'stable' ring - if not documented explicitly, the clinical interventions (angiographic embolization + ex-fix) support reclassification to unstable. Recommendation: recode S32.810A -> S32.811A (MCC) or query surgeon if local coding rules require explicit surgeon stability language. Evidence: ev7 (H&P 'active extravasation'), ev8 (discharge 'IR embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch'), ev17 (H&P problem list 'external fixator placement'). Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851) severity and POA: - What was billed: J95.851 listed on claim with POA=N but flagged as CC. - What the record shows: Infectious Diseases consult documents 'VAP developing shortly after extubation with clinical and radiographic features' and chest radiograph documents new right lower lobe consolidation; discharge summary documents 'hospital-acquired methicillin-susceptible S. aureus ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefazolin' and that extubation was successful on ICU day 9 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n70, n1055) (ev4, ev5, ev10). Policy: J95.851 requires provider confirmation of VAP with timing >48 hours after intubation and carries MCC severity per the governing policy. The record meets the policy validation elements (provider diagnosis of VAP, radiographic infiltrate, clinical criteria, microbiology/targeted antibiotic therapy, and timing >48h). Correction: retain J95.851 but change severity to MCC (policy) and keep POA = N. Evidence: ev4 (ID consult), ev5 (discharge summary), ev10 (extubation on ICU day 9 supports timing and duration >48 hours). Acute kidney injury (N17.9) POA flag: - What was billed: N17.9 POA=N (not present on admission). - What the record shows: The admission H&P (dated on the admit) documents 'Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis-requiring' in the active problem list (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9) (ev3). Nephrology consultation documents CK peak 12,400 and creatinine 2.4 (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n46) (ev9). Those findings meet KDIGO criteria and the provider documents AKI on the early chart. Therefore the POA indicator should be Y (present on admission) rather than N; keep N17.9 as a CC-level diagnosis with POA=Y. Evidence: ev3 (H&P problem list), ev9 (Nephrology consult confirming AKI values). Acute posthemorrhagic anemia (D62) POA flag: - What was billed: D62 POA=N. - What the record shows: Admission laboratories show Hgb 6.8 on arrival (History & Physical laboratory data), and the chart documents massive transfusion (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9) (ev2). Because anemia was documented on arrival (initial Hgb 6.8) it was present on admission and POA should be Y. Evidence: ev2 (admission labs showing Hgb 6.8 (initial)). Other diagnoses/procedures: - Femoral shaft fracture S72.301A is supported by imaging and the operative course (intramedullary nailing) and carries MCC; keep and ensure MCC mapping (NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055) (ev6). - Traumatic pneumothorax / right hemopneumothorax (S27.4XXA) supported by H&P and chest tube placement (ev13). Keep. - Liver laceration S36.115A supported (Grade II, non-operative) (ev14). Keep. - Rhabdomyolysis M62.88 supported on admission (ev3) - keep POA=Y and CC severity as billed. - Right femoral DVT I82.401 supported by progress notes and discharge (ev11) - keep POA=N. - MSSA organism code B95.62 is supported as the causative organism for the documented MSSA VAP and may remain as reported (ev5). - Ventilator procedure 5A1D90Z (assistance >96 consecutive hours) is supported: extubation occurred on ICU day 9 (ev10), consistent with >96 hours; keep procedure and verify procedure-to-chart timing. - Splenectomy procedure (07TP0ZZ) is supported by the operative transfer language (ev1) and discharge course (ev8); keep. Net coding actions required (high level): - Remove unsupported R57.01 (cardiogenic shock). - Reclassify principal diagnosis from contusion of spleen (S36.020A) to the provider-documented splenic laceration (provider-documented Grade IV splenic laceration) - recode principal accordingly (see note below: query coder/physician to select exact laceration ICD-10 7th character matching operative findings). Evidence: ev1, ev15. - Recode pelvic ring injury from S32.810A (stable) to S32.811A (unstable, MCC) given active extravasation and embolization + ex-fix placement, or query surgeon if explicit 'stable' language is required. Evidence: ev7, ev8, ev17. - Correct POA for N17.9 and D62 to Y per admitting documentation (ev3, ev2). - Correct J95.851 severity to MCC (policy validation supported by ID consult + discharge + imaging and treatment) (ev4, ev5, ev10). Evidence citations (selected): ev1: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (History & Physical, admission -> '... transferred to the operating room for damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy, followed by IR embolization for pelvic bleeding.' p.242-475); ev2: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (admit labs -> 'WBC 24.5; Hgb 6.8 (initial); platelets 145; ...'); ev3: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (Active Problem List -> '7 | Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis-requiring' p.242-475); ev4: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n70 (Infectious Diseases consult -> 'VAP developing shortly after extubation with clinical and radiographic features.' p.218); ev5: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055 (Discharge Summary -> 'hospital-acquired methicillin-susceptible S. aureus ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefazolin' p.859); ev6: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055 (Discharge Summary -> 'right femoral shaft fracture requiring intramedullary nailing on ICU day 4' p.859); ev7: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (H&P -> 'pelvic ring injury with active extravasation' p.242-475); ev8: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055 (Discharge Summary -> 'followed by IR embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch.' p.859); ev9: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n46 (Nephrology consult -> 'Rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI with CK peak 12,400 and creatinine 2.4. Adequate urine output with aggressive hydration; no RRT indication.' p.137); ev10: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055 (Discharge Summary -> 'Extubation was successful on ICU day 9 with brief VAP requiring aggressive pulmonary toileting rather than reintubation.' p.859); ev11: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055 (Discharge Summary -> 'catheter-associated right common femoral DVT treated with therapeutic anticoagulation' p.859); ev12: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (H&P -> '5 | Rib fractures (right 4-8) with flail chest physiology' p.242-475); ev13: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (H&P -> '4 | Traumatic right hemopneumothorax status post tube thoracostomy' p.242-475); ev14: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (H&P -> '6 | Grade II liver laceration - non-operative management' p.242-475); ev15: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (H&P Assessment -> '... Grade IV splenic laceration with hemorrhagic shock ...' p.242-475); ev16: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n1055 (Discharge Summary -> 'post-traumatic stress reaction' p.859); ev17: NOTE-Medical-Records-16-30-MR_28.pdf-n9 (H&P Problem List -> '2 | Open-book pelvic ring injury (Tile B1) with external fixator placement' p.242-475). Audit/coder instructions: (1) Query the surgeon and/or trauma attending to confirm the exact ICD-10 splenic laceration code (Grade IV) to replace S36.020A as principal; document the 7th-character and whether the splenic injury was present on admission (the H&P supports POA=Y). (2) Query the orthopedic/trauma surgeon to explicitly document pelvic ring STABILITY (stable vs unstable) if local coding rules require explicit provider statement for unstable classification; if absent, recode to S32.811A given IR embolization for arterial pelvic bleeding and ex-fix placement. (3) Remove R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) - no supporting documentation. (4) Correct POA flags for N17.9 and D62 to Y; update J95.851 to MCC in the coding map. (5) Maintain all operative/procedure codes listed (splenectomy, IMN, ex-fix, IR embolization, chest tube, prolonged ventilation >96h) as supported by the operative/transfer/discharge narrative (ev1, ev6, ev8, ev13, ev10).
result.rationale_letter: Re: Clinical coding audit of inpatient stay MR_28 (admit 10/30/2026-discharge 03/02/2027) Dear Provider/Health Record Team, We reviewed the documentation and coding for the above admission (Level 1 trauma after high-speed MVC). The review compared billed diagnosis/procedure lines against the medical record and applicable coding policies. Based on the chart, we have determined there are coding errors that require correction. The principal issues and corrective actions are summarized below. Finding: Principal diagnosis sequencing and unsupported diagnosis - Basis: The admitting History & Physical and the discharge summary document a Grade IV splenic LACERATION with hemorrhagic shock and state the patient underwent emergent damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy (History & Physical; Discharge/Transfer Summary). The claim currently lists S36.020A (contusion of spleen) as the principal diagnosis. The contusion code does not match the provider-documented splenic laceration and operative splenectomy that occasioned admission and definitive surgical treatment. (Evidence: History & Physical - transfer to OR for damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy; Discharge Summary - status post splenectomy.) - Correction required: Principal diagnosis should reflect the provider-documented splenic laceration (the appropriate ICD-10 laceration code per the operative findings). Please update the principal diagnosis to the splenic laceration code consistent with operative documentation (Grade IV; include correct 7th character). Also retain Z90.81 (acquired absence of spleen) as a secondary code for post-splenectomy status. Finding: Unsupported cardiogenic shock code (R57.01) - Basis: The chart documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock and activation of massive transfusion; there is no documentation of cardiogenic shock (no cardiology assessment, echo findings, or ischemic event described). (Evidence: H&P assessment listing hemorrhagic shock and MTP activation.) - Correction required: Remove R57.01 from the claim. Finding: Pelvic ring fracture severity and coding - Basis: The record documents pelvic ring injury with active arterial extravasation requiring IR embolization and external fixation. Policy and coding guidance distinguish stable vs unstable pelvic ring disruption; unstable injuries (S32.811A) carry higher severity (MCC) and are associated with arterial bleeding/embolization and operative stabilization. (Evidence: H&P 'pelvic ring injury with active extravasation'; Discharge/Transfer Summary 'IR embolization of a bleeding right internal iliac branch'; H&P: external fixator placement.) - Correction required: Reclassify pelvic ring disruption to S32.811A (unstable) unless the treating surgeon explicitly documents 'stable' - if explicit 'stable' language exists, retain S32.810A; otherwise code as S32.811A (MCC). Finding: Ventilator-associated pneumonia severity (J95.851) - Basis: Infectious Diseases consultation documents confirmed VAP developing post-extubation with radiographic consolidation; discharge documents MSSA VAP treated with cefazolin; extubation was on ICU day 9 (well beyond 48 hours). The governing VAP policy requires provider confirmation and timing >48 hours post-intubation; when criteria met J95.851 is assigned and carries MCC. (Evidence: ID consult, discharge summary, extubation on ICU day 9.) - Correction required: Retain J95.851 but map it as MCC (not CC) and ensure POA = N. Finding: POA flag corrections for AKI and acute posthemorrhagic anemia - Basis: Admission H&P documents 'Rhabdomyolysis with acute kidney injury (KDIGO 2), non-dialysis-requiring' and the admit labs include Hgb 6.8 on arrival. These findings indicate AKI and post-hemorrhagic anemia were present on admission. (Evidence: H&P problem list; admission labs.) - Correction required: Set N17.9 POA = Y and D62 POA = Y. Procedures: The operative and procedural coding (splenectomy 07TP0ZZ, IMN of right femur, pelvic external fixation, IR embolization 04L33DZ, chest tube/pleural device, central access, prolonged ventilation >96 hours 5A1D90Z, blood transfusions) are supported in the record and may be retained as billed. (Evidence: H&P operative transfer language; discharge summary describing IMN and ex-fix; extubation on ICU day 9 for ventilation duration; IR embolization described.) Requested actions: 1) Recode principal diagnosis to the provider-documented splenic laceration code (per operative findings) and retain Z90.81 as appropriate. 2) Remove R57.01 (cardiogenic shock). 3) Reclassify pelvic ring fracture to unstable (S32.811A) or query surgeon if explicit stability wording is required. 4) Change J95.851 severity to MCC (POA=N). 5) Set N17.9 and D62 POA=Y. 6) Maintain the listed operative/procedure codes (splenectomy, IMN, ex-fix, IR embolization, chest tube, prolonged ventilation >96h, transfusion) as supported. If you disagree with any of these proposed coding actions, please provide the specific chart documentation (operative note, attending surgeon stability statement for the pelvis, cardiology consultation supporting cardiogenic shock, or explicit contrary timing/lab data) so we may reassess. Thank you for your cooperation. Sincerely, Clinical Coding Audit Team

code_decisions.reason: Admission H&P and operative course document a Grade IV splenic LACERATION with emergent splenectomy; contusion (S36.020A) does not match provider-documented laceration that occasioned the surgery. Recode principal to the splenic laceration code and retain post-splenectomy status as secondary; query surgeon if necessary to confirm exact laceration 7th character.
Right femoral shaft fracture is documented with intramedullary nailing (operative course); policy supports S72.301A as MCC when treated with IMN.

Chart documents pelvic ring injury with active arterial extravasation requiring IR embolization and external fixation, which supports reclassification to unstable pelvic ring disruption (S32.811A, MCC). If surgeon documents 'stable' explicitly, retain original; otherwise recode to S32.811A.
Traumatic right hemopneumothorax with tube thoracostomy is documented on admission; supports traumatic pneumothorax diagnosis and related procedure(s).
Grade II liver laceration is documented and managed non-operatively in the record.
No documentation supports cardiogenic shock; record documents hemorrhagic/traumatic shock with massive transfusion rather than cardiogenic etiology.
Traumatic/hemorrhagic shock from splenic injury is documented on admission and treated with damage-control resuscitation.
Rhabdomyolysis documented on admission with high CK and AKI; supports M62.88 and its CC mapping.
AKI is documented in the admission H&P (KDIGO 2) and confirmed by nephrology (creatinine 2.4); therefore POA should be Y and the CC diagnosis is supported.

Provider-documented VAP with supporting radiograph/clinical deterioration, organism identification (MSSA) and targeted therapy meets policy validation for J95.851; per policy this is MCC and must carry POA = N.
Discharge and treatment documentation identify MSSA as the organism for the VAP; retain the organism code with POA = N.
Right femoral/common femoral DVT is documented and treated with therapeutic anticoagulation; retain as a CC-level diagnosis with POA = N.
Post-traumatic stress reaction is documented in the discharge diagnoses; retain as secondary diagnosis (POA as documented).
Admission hemoglobin was 6.8 (initial); anemia due to hemorrhage was present on admission and POA should be Y.
Post-splenectomy status is documented in operative and discharge notes; POA = N (acquired during this admission).
Endotracheal tube insertion and intubation documented on arrival (H&P); procedural support present.
Splenectomy is documented as performed emergently in the operative/damage-control course.
Pleural/hemopneumothorax management including thoracostomy is documented.
IR embolization of a right internal iliac branch for pelvic hemorrhage is documented; code for arterial occlusion is supported.
External fixation of the pelvis is documented (ex-fix placed); retain procedure code.
External fixation device insertion into right upper femur documented as part of staged orthopedics/damage-control management.
Repair of right femoral shaft with IM nail is documented (definitive fixation performed).
Transfusion(s) documented in the operative and post-op course (massive transfusion products noted); retain transfusion code.
Central venous access into SVC is listed on claim and is consistent with ICU-level care; supporting line documentation should be retained in the chart.
Assistance with mechanical ventilation >96 consecutive hours is supported: extubation occurred on ICU day 9, consistent with >96 hours of support.
